label: first copy step echoing a/i in long sequences followed by s/d/b
predicate: (recall_idx == 1) & isin(first_tok, [tok("a"), tok("i")]) & (L >= 8) & isin(orig(1), [tok("s"), tok("d"), tok("b"), tok("m"), tok("i")]) & isin(orig(2), [tok("s"), tok("d"), tok("b"), tok("l"), tok("w"), tok("m"), tok("a")])
explanation: Very sparse feature (about 0.003% of steps). It fires only at step L+1, where the input is the echoed first token and the model outputs original token 1. Nothing fires in the original or delimiter phases, or at any other copy position. About 90% of activations (and of activation mass) have first token a or i, and almost all the rest have m, 2, b or l. It is stronger in long sequences: L=9 holds 63% of the mass and it never fires for L<=5. It also prefers the next original tokens (orig 1 and 2) to come from {s,d,b,m,l,w}. The core gate (recall_idx==1 and first token a/i) reaches about 90% recall but under 1% precision. Adding the length and orig(1)/orig(2) conditions gives F1 about 0.34 on dev. So the feature is a sparse conjunction of first token and the next few tokens that these conditions only partly capture. All top examples have first token a or i and orig(1) in {s,d}; I did not test magnitude any further.
